grammar:alternative-question-a-or-b.title: 选择疑问句 Are you A or B?
grammar:alternative-question-a-or-b.explanation: 在 be 动词后直接跟两个并列选项 A or B，构成选择疑问句，语气比一般疑问句更具体，让对方二选一。
grammar:alternative-question-a-or-b.source: Are you a night owl or an early bird?
grammar:alternative-question-a-or-b.example: Do you prefer tea or coffee?

grammar:can-i-get-you-offer-food-drink.title: Can I get you...? 主动提供食物饮料
grammar:can-i-get-you-offer-food-drink.explanation: Can I get you...? 是口语中主动问别人要不要某物的自然句型，常用于主人待客、餐厅服务或朋友之间拿饮料食物。
grammar:can-i-get-you-offer-food-drink.example: Can I get you some coffee or orange juice?

grammar:comma-appositive-renaming.title: 用逗号连接的同位语结构（具体名称点明前文所指）
grammar:comma-appositive-renaming.explanation: 名词短语 + 逗号 + 具体名称，后者是前者的同位语，说明“……正是……”。The last hidden world, China 意为“最后的隐秘之地——正是中国”。这种结构适合先抛概念再点名，语气偏书面，常见于标题、纪录片解说或隆重介绍。
grammar:comma-appositive-renaming.example: My dream city, Paris, never fails to amaze me. → 我梦想的城市巴黎，总让我惊叹。

grammar:compound-adjective-time-duration.title: 时间长度作定语时常用连字符复合形容词
grammar:compound-adjective-time-duration.explanation: 当时间长度放在名词前面作定语时，英语常把它压缩成复合形容词，通常用单数并加连字符，如 a ten-minute rest、a two-hour meeting。重点是它整体修饰后面的名词，而不是把 minutes 当作普通复数名词直接去修饰 rest。
grammar:compound-adjective-time-duration.example: After a ten-minute rest, she felt better.

grammar:continue-complements-and-registe.title: continue：后接结构、continue on 与 proceed 的分工
grammar:continue-complements-and-registe.explanation: continue doing 与 continue to do 都表示「继续做某事」，强调动作或活动的延续；continue with + 名词 用于继续某项活动、流程或内容（continue with the presentation）。continue on 强调沿当前路线、方向继续前进（Continue on for another two miles），也可表示接着进入下一阶段（continue on to the next section），但不带「办理某项事务」的含义，办某件事要用 proceed with + 名词。proceed 更正式，常见于交通指示、公告与流程说明：proceed to + 地点或动词原形，proceed with + 事情或计划。交通语境说 When the light turns green, we can continue on；continue on 已含继续向前，不必再加 ahead，after green light 也不自然，应用 when / after the light turns green。叙述已发生的动作时，continue 要用过去式 continued，并与整体过去时态保持一致。
grammar:continue-complements-and-registe.source: continue doing, continue to do, continue with, proceed to, proceed with
grammar:continue-complements-and-registe.example: After a short break, we continued discussing the plan, then continued on to the budget.

grammar:could-you-polite-request.title: Could you...? 礼貌请求
grammar:could-you-polite-request.explanation: Could you...? 常用来礼貌地请别人做事，比直接用 Do it 或 Can you...? 更柔和，适合家庭、朋友和服务场景。
grammar:could-you-polite-request.example: Could you slice the bread while I pour the coffee?

grammar:do-you-think-we-can.title: Do you think we can...?（委婉征求意见句型）
grammar:do-you-think-we-can.explanation: 用 Do you think + 主语 + can + 动词原形，把请求包装成你觉得是否可行，比直接的 Can we...? 更委婉，适合礼貌地提建议或请求。回答可用 Yes, I think so. / I'm afraid not.
grammar:do-you-think-we-can.source: Do you think we can make a pit stop?
grammar:do-you-think-we-can.example: Do you think we can finish this by five?（你觉得我们五点前能做完吗？）

grammar:drive-object-up-by-amount.title: drive / boost + 宾语 + up by + 幅度：表提升量的结构
grammar:drive-object-up-by-amount.explanation: 表“把某指标推高多少”用 drive/boost/push + 宾语 + up + by + 幅度：by 引出变化量，不能省略；up 可放在宾语前（drive up sales）或宾语后（drive sales up），但宾语是代词时必须后置（drive them up）。若要说明变化的起点或终点，可换 from ... to ...。注意不能写成 drive sales up 20%，幅度前必须有 by。
grammar:drive-object-up-by-amount.example: A single viral video drove up sign-ups by 30% overnight.

grammar:first-then-action-sequence.title: first, then 表示动作顺序
grammar:first-then-action-sequence.explanation: first, then 用来清楚安排两个先后动作，适合做饭、计划、说明步骤等场景；first 放在第一个动作后或句首都可以，then 引出下一步。
grammar:first-then-action-sequence.source: Sure. I’ll slice the bread first, then pour the juice.
grammar:first-then-action-sequence.example: I’ll wash the vegetables first, then chop them.

grammar:gerund-as-subject.title: Gerund phrase as sentence subject
grammar:gerund-as-subject.explanation: When an action itself is the subject of a clause, use the gerund (-ing) form, not the bare infinitive. 'Sacrificing your personal life' functions as a singular subject, so the verb agrees as singular (is, not are). The whole gerund phrase carries its own object ('your personal life').
grammar:gerund-as-subject.source: sacrificing your personal life is a pretty big price to pay
grammar:gerund-as-subject.example: Working from home has both advantages and disadvantages.

grammar:get-down-to-preposition.title: get down to + 名词/动名词：开始认真做某事
grammar:get-down-to-preposition.explanation: get down to 里的 to 是介词而非不定式标记，所以后面接名词或动名词（-ing），不能接动词原形。这是高频易错点：要说 get down to doing/working，而不是 get down to do。整句结构：Let's get down to + 任务。可用于 get down to work / get down to the details / get down to planning。
grammar:get-down-to-preposition.example: We need to get down to writing the report today.

grammar:have-got-possession-present.title: have got 表示现在拥有
grammar:have-got-possession-present.explanation: 口语中 have got 可表示现在拥有或具备，I've got 与 I have 在此句中的意思基本相同；形式上包含 have 和过去分词 got，但整句强调现在的处境，并非强调刚刚得到。
grammar:have-got-possession-present.source: I've got my whole life ahead of me.
grammar:have-got-possession-present.example: I've got plenty of time to decide.

grammar:ill-volunteer-to-do-something.title: I’ll... 主动承担任务
grammar:ill-volunteer-to-do-something.explanation: I’ll 加动词原形可以表示说话人当场决定或主动承担某个任务，常用于分工、帮忙和即时回应。
grammar:ill-volunteer-to-do-something.example: I’ll stir the eggs while you make the toast.

grammar:infinitive-postmodifier-active-f.title: 主动不定式后置修饰名词时表被动意义
grammar:infinitive-postmodifier-active-f.explanation: 名词后接主动形式的不定式（a price to pay, a lot of work to do, nothing to worry about）时，不定式作后置定语，逻辑上却是被动的：相当于 a price that must be paid。因为承受者在语境中已明确，英语不再额外加被动标记；写成 a price to be paid 只有在需要强调“将由某人支付”、承受者未定时才更合适。
grammar:infinitive-postmodifier-active-f.source: There is a price to pay for that kind of fame.
grammar:infinitive-postmodifier-active-f.example: There is a price to pay for that kind of fame, and a lot of work to do before it arrives.

grammar:may-condition-if.title: may + 动词与 if 条件从句
grammar:may-condition-if.explanation: may suffer 表示可能发生；if 引导条件从句，说明产生这种可能结果的条件。一般事实或现实可能条件中，if 从句常用一般现在时。
grammar:may-condition-if.source: A young man may suffer from the green-eyed monster if his girlfriend begins going out with someone else
grammar:may-condition-if.example: You may feel nervous if you speak in public for the first time.

grammar:mean-that-object-clause.title: mean 后接宾语从句
grammar:mean-that-object-clause.explanation: mean 后可直接接省略 that 的宾语从句，说明某个标志、事实或行为所表示的含义。
grammar:mean-that-object-clause.source: A green light on a traffic signal means your car can continue on
grammar:mean-that-object-clause.example: A flashing light means you should slow down.

grammar:no-way-that-clause.title: There's no way (that) + 从句：同位语从句与否定范围
grammar:no-way-that-clause.explanation: There is no way that + 完整句子：that 从句说明 way（可能性）的具体内容，属同位语从句，口语常省略 that；从句用陈述语序。no way 已经把「不可能」放在句首，所以从句内部仍用肯定形式，不能再套一层否定。
grammar:no-way-that-clause.source: There's no way I'm gonna eat this.
grammar:no-way-that-clause.example: There's no way she'll finish the report by Friday.（她绝不可能在周五前写完报告。）

grammar:now-discourse-marker.title: Now 用作讲解开场
grammar:now-discourse-marker.explanation: 句首 Now 可以不是时间副词“现在”，而是话语标记，用来把听者注意力拉到接下来要解释的内容上，语气像“那么/注意”。
grammar:now-discourse-marker.source: Now, to dish up something means...
grammar:now-discourse-marker.example: Now, this expression is usually used in casual conversation.

grammar:participial-phrase-logical-subje.title: 分词短语的逻辑主语
grammar:participial-phrase-logical-subje.explanation: 句首分词短语没有明写主语时，其动作的执行者通常必须与主句主语一致；否则容易形成悬垂修饰语。
grammar:participial-phrase-logical-subje.source: After reviewing the safety report, officials have decided to proceed with the project next Monday.
grammar:participial-phrase-logical-subje.example: After checking the map, we chose a different route.

grammar:past-perfect-before-past-referen.title: 过去完成时表示过去参照点之前
grammar:past-perfect-before-past-referen.explanation: had just arrived 表示“刚刚到达”发生在 used it to describe 这一过去行为之前；just 强调时间间隔很短。
grammar:past-perfect-before-past-referen.source: Old-timers used it to describe a man who had just arrived from one of the big cities back east
grammar:past-perfect-before-past-referen.example: They welcomed a traveler who had just arrived from Boston.

grammar:prefer-x-rather-than-y.title: prefer X rather than Y：比起 Y 更喜欢 X（平行结构）
grammar:prefer-x-rather-than-y.explanation: prefer A to B is the most compact pattern (prefer tea to coffee). prefer X rather than Y also works to contrast two options; X and Y must be grammatically parallel (both nouns, both gerunds, both full clauses). In the source sentence X = a night of playing cards with friends, Y = a loud and crazy dance party, two noun phrases kept parallel. Avoid mixing a gerund with a bare noun after rather than.
grammar:prefer-x-rather-than-y.source: prefer a night of playing cards with friends rather than a loud and crazy dance party
grammar:prefer-x-rather-than-y.example: I prefer staying in and cooking rather than going out to a crowded restaurant.

grammar:prepositional-phrase-sentence-fu.title: 介词短语在句子中的作用和成分
grammar:prepositional-phrase-sentence-fu.explanation: 介词通常不能单独充当完整成分，而是和名词、代词、动名词等组成介词短语，用来说明时间、地点、方向、原因、方式、对象、所属关系等。介词短语在句中常作状语、后置定语、表语、宾语补足语，少数情况下也可作主语补语或名词/形容词/动词的补足成分。
grammar:prepositional-phrase-sentence-fu.source: 介词的作用是什么，在句子结构中通常充当什么成分
grammar:prepositional-phrase-sentence-fu.example: She left after lunch. / The book on the desk is mine. / He is in trouble.

grammar:present-participle-as-adj.title: 现在分词作形容词：表示主动、正在进行的特征
grammar:present-participle-as-adj.explanation: V-ing 形式作定语/表语时表示「主动且正在进行的性质」，如 steaming forests = forests that are steaming（正冒着蒸汽的森林）。与之相对，过去分词 -ed 表示被动或已完成的状态（a steamed bun 蒸好的包子）。可迁移到 boiling water（沸腾的水）/ boiled water（烧开过的水）、running water 等。
grammar:present-participle-as-adj.source: steaming forests（正在冒蒸汽的森林）
grammar:present-participle-as-adj.example: Boiling water is dangerous, but boiled water is safe to drink.

grammar:present-perfect-for-duration.title: 现在完成时 + for 时间段：从过去持续到现在的反复动作
grammar:present-perfect-for-duration.explanation: For centuries, travellers to China have told tales... 中 have told 是现在完成时，搭配 for centuries 表示'几个世纪以来一直如此'，即动作在过去开始、反复发生并延续到现在。现在完成时强调'到目前为止'的累计/持续，而非具体过去时间点。
grammar:present-perfect-for-duration.source: For Centuries, travellers to China have told tales of magical landscapes and surprising creatures.
grammar:present-perfect-for-duration.example: People have told stories about this mountain for hundreds of years. (几百年来人们一直在讲述这座山的故事。)

grammar:purpose-infinitive-to.title: to + 动词原形：表目的的目的状语
grammar:purpose-infinitive-to.explanation: to match… 是目的不定式，回答「做这件事是为了什么」，相当于 in order to / so as to + 动词原形，但更轻便，书面和口语都常用。它不占句子主干：句子已经有谓语（如 cut the fee），to do 只附加说明目的一侧，位置可在句末也可提到句首（句首时更常用 in order to）。否定写 in order not to / so as not to，不写 to not do。目的不定式默认与句子主语同指，主语不一致时要改成 so that + 主语 + 情态动词；接名词或从句时同样用 so that。
grammar:purpose-infinitive-to.example: He checked the receipt in order not to get overcharged.

grammar:range-from-to.title: range from A to B / ranging from...to...
grammar:range-from-to.explanation: range from A to B 表示范围从 A 到 B；句中 ranging from... 是现在分词短语作后置定语，相当于 which range from...，修饰 vast deserts。这是纪录片、说明文常用的区间概括句型。
grammar:range-from-to.source: Vast deserts ranging from searing hot to mind-numbing cold.
grammar:range-from-to.example: The region’s climates range from tropical monsoon to arid desert.（该地区的气候从热带季风到干旱沙漠不一而同。）

grammar:shouldnt-negative-expectation.title: shouldn't：表示预计某事不会发生
grammar:shouldnt-negative-expectation.explanation: shouldn't + 动词除了可以表示不应该做某事，还可以根据上下文表达说话人的判断：按目前情况看，某事预计不会发生。This drizzle shouldn't cause much trouble 表示说话人预计这点毛毛雨不会造成太大麻烦，并非在谈义务或禁止。
grammar:shouldnt-negative-expectation.source: This drizzle shouldn't cause much trouble.
grammar:shouldnt-negative-expectation.example: The delay shouldn't affect our plans.

grammar:since-then-perfect-tense.title: since then 表“从那时起”须搭配完成时
grammar:since-then-perfect-tense.explanation: since then 划定一个从过去某点延续到现在的时间段，谓语通常用现在完成时或现在完成进行时；只叙述两次先后动作时不能用它替代 later。
grammar:since-then-perfect-tense.source: Since then, I have worked in three different studios.
grammar:since-then-perfect-tense.example: Since then, I have worked in three different studios.

grammar:surprising-surprised.title: -ing 形容词 surprising（令人…的）vs -ed 形容词 surprised（感到…的）
grammar:surprising-surprised.explanation: surprising 形容'令人惊讶的事物'（修饰物/事件），surprised 形容'感到惊讶的人'（修饰人）。surprising creatures 意为'令人惊讶的生物'，说明这些生物本身让人惊讶。
grammar:surprising-surprised.source: ...tales of magical landscapes and surprising creatures.
grammar:surprising-surprised.example: The news was surprising, and I was really surprised. (这个消息令人惊讶，我真的很吃惊。)

grammar:the-smell-of-noun.title: the smell of + 名词 表“…的气味”
grammar:the-smell-of-noun.explanation: 用 of 引出气味来源，“the smell of smoke”比名词复合形式更自然、正式；口语中也常说 smells like smoke。
grammar:the-smell-of-noun.source: I cannot stand the smell of smoke.
grammar:the-smell-of-noun.example: The smell of fresh bread filled the room.

grammar:we-will-contraction.title: We'll = We will：表将来/计划
grammar:we-will-contraction.explanation: 口语中 will 与主语缩写为 'll，读 /wiːl/。用于表达将来的动作、临时决定或承诺，语气比 be going to 更即时。这里表示“我们稍后会再谈这个话题”。
grammar:we-will-contraction.source: We'll talk about that a little bit later on.
grammar:we-will-contraction.example: We'll call you when we get home. / 我们到家后给你打电话。

grammar:what-clause-as-predicative.title: what 引导的表语从句
grammar:what-clause-as-predicative.explanation: You are what you eat 的主干是「主语 You + 系动词 are + 表语」。这里的表语不是名词或形容词，而是一个从句 what you eat，所以叫表语从句。what 在从句内部充当 eat 的宾语（eat what → what you eat），同时把整个从句「名词化」，让它能站在系动词后面。这和 that 引导的表语从句不同：that 只起连接作用、不充当成分；what 必须在从句里当成分（主语或宾语）。
grammar:what-clause-as-predicative.example: You are what you repeatedly do. / The problem is what he said yesterday.

grammar:while-clause-simultaneous-action.title: while 从句表示同时动作
grammar:while-clause-simultaneous-action.explanation: while 可以连接两个同时发生的动作，结构常见为 do something while someone does something，用来说明分工或背景动作。
grammar:while-clause-simultaneous-action.source: No problem. I'll stir the eggs while you make the toast.
grammar:while-clause-simultaneous-action.example: I’ll wash the cups while you set the table.
